glossary.definition: Delegation: the agent presents its own token as the actor, and the ID-JAG records it in an act claim. may_act on the ID token says who may act for the user.
Client ID Metadata Document: a client_id that is an HTTPS URL pointing to the client's metadata, so no registration step is needed. PingFederate 13.1 supports it.
Sender-constrained tokens: the token carries cnf.jkt and every call proves possession of the matching key. PingFederate 13.1 turns it on per client.
The MCP specification extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/enterprise-managed-authorization) that applies ID-JAG to MCP clients and servers. VS Code and mcpc implement it as clients.

Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant: a short-lived JWT (typ oauth-id-jag+jwt) that an IdP signs for one client and one target authorization server, so the client can get an access token there without a new user sign-in.
Proof of the user's sign-in that the client trades for an ID-JAG: an OpenID Connect ID token, a SAML 2.0 assertion, or a refresh token.
The enterprise IdP (here PingFederate) that signs the user in, applies policy and issues ID-JAGs. It is where an administrator decides which app may reach which other app.
Each ID-JAG is redeemed at most once. The resource authorization server remembers issuer plus jti until the assertion expires and refuses a second use.
The grant the client uses at the resource authorization server to trade the ID-JAG for an access token: grant_type jwt-bearer with the ID-JAG as the assertion.
Pushed authorization requests (RFC 9126) and rich authorization requests (RFC 9396, authorization_details). Both appear in the cross-domain variant of the flow.
Revoking the user's refresh token at the IdP (RFC 7009) stops new ID-JAGs from that session. Access tokens already minted stay valid until they expire.
The client or AI agent that wants to call another app on the user's behalf. In the playground it is this app's server; mcpc and VS Code are real ones.
The target app's authorization server. It validates the ID-JAG and issues its own access token; the ID-JAG's aud must equal its issuer exactly.
The REST API or MCP server that accepts the resource authorization server's access token, checking issuer, audience, expiry and scope.
This kit's rule: a trusted IdP may mint only for the client IDs mapped to it in the registry, and the ID-JAG's client_id must map to the client redeeming it.
An optional structured subject in the ID-JAG, for example a SAML NameID together with its issuer, so two IdPs that use the same NameID never collide.
The grant the client uses at the IdP to get an ID-JAG: grant_type token-exchange with requested_token_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag, plus audience and resource.
Okta's product name for the ID-JAG pattern. Same protocol; PingFederate's documentation does not use the name.

cards.label: Why it matters: the gateway redeems the ID-JAG (DRAFT, Ping claims unverified)
cards.description: DRAFT by the lab author, not Ping wording; the owner replaces it. Ping release claim (2026-11-02), UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: Agents often reach other apps through a separate consent screen for each app, which the company's identity provider does not see, or through a static API key that carries no user context. Either way, it is hard to tie the agent's access to a specific user. Technical: The gateway trades the caller's token for an ID-JAG (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant), a signed statement that this user may access the other app. When a Redeem setting with a token URL is configured, the gateway presents it to that app's own authorization server to get an access token for the user; without Redeem, it is not presented. Business: The app receives a token issued for the individual user, not for an identity shared by every user, so it can tie its access to that user, and it still applies its own policy at its own authorization server. ID-JAG is still an IETF draft and may change.
